summary: Plan on Chiang Mai’s regular Sunday Walking Street on 6 December, with a useful overlap with the officially dated Chiang Mai Design Week (5–13 December 2026). The weekly market is a recurring event rather than a separately announced one-off for this date; the exact 2026 operating arrangements and any Design Week market tie-in are not confirmed.
whyGo: Ratchadamnoen Road’s roughly 1 km pedestrian market is a lively sampler of Chiang Mai handicrafts, local food and small makers.

Design Week is officially scheduled across this Sunday, creating a good chance to combine the street market with the city’s design festival, whose programme includes exhibitions, creative markets, music and community events. Specific nearby Sunday events may change as the programme develops.
bestFor: An easy evening of browsing, snacks and people-watching in the Old City.
Visitors already in Chiang Mai for Design Week who want a less structured festival evening.
skipIf: You dislike dense crowds, slow-moving pedestrian traffic or shopping-focused evenings.
You need a quiet or reliably step-free route; narrow, crowded sections and uneven street surfaces can be difficult.
duration: Allow 1.5–3 hours for a short browse and food stops; the full market route can take longer in crowds. Planning estimate.
cost: No entry fee is indicated; food, drinks, crafts and optional services are pay-as-you-go. Bring small Thai baht notes. Individual prices vary.
hours: The Tourism Authority of Thailand’s Japanese-language visitor listing gives Sundays approximately 17:00–24:00. Treat this as usual guidance; exact hours and road closure timing for 6 December 2026 are unconfirmed.
bestTime: Arrive around opening for easier movement, or later for the evening atmosphere. Expect unusually high demand because Design Week is also running; that crowd effect is a planning inference, not a published forecast.
gettingThere: The market is on Ratchadamnoen Road in the Old City, extending from Tha Phae Gate toward Wat Phra Singh. Walk from nearby Old City accommodation; arrange a drop-off at the edge of the closure and expect to walk. Confirm pickup points locally because traffic restrictions may apply.
booking: No ticket or advance booking is listed for the street market. Design Week listings may have separate registration or ticket rules for individual activities; check the official programme before attending a specific event.
accessibility: The road becomes pedestrian-only during the market, but crowd density, curb transitions and uneven surfaces may make wheelchair or mobility-aid travel challenging. No official accessibility information for this date was found.
practicalTips: Agree on a meeting point and pickup location before entering; phone reception and navigation can be awkward in a dense crowd.
Carry cash and a reusable water bottle; check individual stall payment options.
Keep valuables secure and ask before photographing vendors or their work.
Use the Design Week official programme for confirmed venue and event details closer to the date.
decemberNotes: Chiang Mai Design Week 2026 is officially scheduled for 5–13 December, so 6 December falls within the festival. The Sunday Walking Street is listed as a weekly Sunday market, making its operation on that date a reasonable expectation, but no source located explicitly confirms a special 6 December market edition or coordination with the festival. Verify local notices shortly before travel.
uncertainties: The market’s recurring Sunday schedule is documented, but the 6 December 2026 edition’s exact hours, closure limits and any cancellation are not separately announced in the sources reviewed.

Design Week confirms 5–13 December, but the current programme page did not expose individual listings during research; do not assume a particular event, stall or festival zone will be on the market route.
Accessibility conditions and stall prices vary and were not published for this date.
